svg.title: CSSV demo
svg.desc: A CSSV file is typed into an editor, and the table rendered from it follows each change. The file starts as plain CSV. An imported stylesheet turns the table into a split-flap departures board. Rules on the sign classes give each delay a remark: on time, delayed, early or cancelled. --cssv-key names the rows, and one rule shows Boarding for flight LH 441. Typing a delay for the cancelled flight changes its remark, and deleting it cancels the flight again. Deleting the style block returns the plain table.

g.text: Any CSV file is already a CSSV file.
Put CSS on top, between --- lines. This file imports a board style.
The sign of each delay picks its remark: .zero, .positive, .negative, :empty.
--cssv-key names each row, so CSS can pick out one flight.
Change the data and the board follows. The CSS stays the same.
Delete the style block and it’s plain CSV again.
